newsitem.title: GERMANY: Japan's Mitsuzuka pledges policies boosting demand.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Mitsuzuka pledges policies boosting demand.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Saturday promised U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that Tokyo would continue to direct its policies primarily toward promoting strong domestic demand, a U.S. treasury official said.
The official, speaking to reporters after a bilateral meeting between the U.S. and Japanese officials at the G7 summit, said that Rubin welcomed the Japanese efforts.
The spokesman declined to comment when asked if the two men had discussed foreign exchange.

"Minister Mitsuzuka stated that the Japanese government would carefully monitor the Japanese economic situation and would continue to direct policies primarily towards ensuring strong domestic-demand-led growth."
Mitsuzuka also told Rubin about plans to reform Japan's financial system including the foreign exchange control law, the spokesman said.
"Rubin welcomed these efforts," the spokesman said.
Rubin and Mitsuzuka met ahead of meetings with the world's seven most industrialised nations here. The U.S. Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain are members of the G7.
